moreContext:
Eightfold AI is a talent intelligence platform that large employers use to match people to jobs by skills, run AI-led screening interviews and plan internal mobility. Founded in 2016, it built its reputation on a deep-learning model trained on large volumes of career data, and has since added AI agents that do recruiting work directly. It positions itself as human-led: agents gather and summarize signal, while recruiters and managers make the decisions.

## What is Eightfold AI used for?

HR and talent acquisition teams use Eightfold to hire faster, find internal candidates for open roles and understand the skills in their workforce.

- Matching applicants and past candidates to open roles based on skills and career trajectories
- Running AI Interviewer screening interviews for invited candidates around the clock
- Supporting live interviews with the AI Interview Companion
- Guiding applicants through the process with a Candidate Agent
- Managing internal mobility, career paths and contingent workforce staffing
- Building custom HR apps and agents on TalentForge

## Who Eightfold AI is best for

Eightfold suits large enterprises and public sector organizations with big applicant volumes and a strategic focus on skills-based hiring and internal mobility. Its frontline hiring features also serve employers filling many hourly roles. Small and mid-sized companies without an HR technology team will likely find it too large and should consider simpler sourcing or screening tools.

## Eightfold AI pricing

Eightfold AI does not publish pricing, and there is no public pricing page as of October 2026. Buyers register for a live demo or request one from sales, and contracts are scoped by modules, employee count and hiring volume. An agentic ROI calculator on the site helps estimate impact before talking to sales.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- No public pricing or self-serve option
- Implementation touches many HR systems and takes time
- Skills inferences need human review, especially for unusual career paths
- AI in hiring is regulated in some regions, so compliance review is important

## Eightfold AI vs alternatives

Coo by Cooper is a lighter option if sourcing qualified candidates against a hiring brief is your main need. Talynce suits smaller teams that want resume ranking, AI voice screening and video interviews without an enterprise rollout. Workleap is a better fit for people management, performance reviews and engagement rather than recruiting. Eightfold AI wins for enterprises that want one skills-based platform covering external hiring, AI interviews and internal mobility.

## Tips for getting started with Eightfold AI

Clean up your job architecture and skills taxonomy before rollout, since matching quality depends on it. Start with one use case, such as rediscovering past applicants for open roles, to show value quickly. Review Eightfold's published bias audit results with your legal team. Train recruiters on how to read match explanations so they use them as input, not verdicts.

## Eightfold AI FAQ

Q: Is Eightfold AI free?
A: No. Eightfold AI is an enterprise platform with no free plan or published pricing; quotes come through a demo.

Q: What is Eightfold AI used for?
A: Eightfold AI is used for skills-based hiring, AI screening interviews, talent management and internal mobility at large organizations.

Q: Is Eightfold AI's hiring AI audited for bias?
A: Yes. Eightfold publishes bias audit results for its AI Interviewer and matching model and lists ISO/IEC 42001 certification.

Q: What is the best alternative to Eightfold AI?
A: Coo by Cooper is a lighter alternative for AI sourcing, while Talynce suits smaller teams needing AI screening and interviews.

Virtual Staging AI is an AI virtual staging tool that lets real estate agents upload a photo of a room and get back a furnished, listing-ready image in seconds. It was developed at the Harvard Innovation Lab and focuses on one job: staging rooms quickly and cheaply while keeping walls, windows and floors as they are. That narrow focus, plus unlimited regenerations, is its main difference from general AI interior design apps.

## What is Virtual Staging AI used for?

Agents and photographers use Virtual Staging AI to make vacant or dated rooms look lived in for online listings, flyers and social posts, without paying for physical staging.

- Furnishing empty bedrooms, living rooms, kitchens and other room types from a single photo
- Removing existing furniture and clutter before adding new pieces
- Switching between design styles such as modern, Scandinavian or industrial
- Regenerating a room as many times as needed until the result fits the listing
- Downloading watermark-free images for MLS, portals and marketing
- Connecting the Enterprise plan's API to a brokerage or photography workflow

## Who Virtual Staging AI is best for

It is built for listing agents, real estate teams, brokerages and property photographers who handle vacant homes or new builds regularly. Property managers marketing empty rentals can use it too. Interior designers who need detailed, product-accurate renders, or buyers wanting a full remodel concept, will want a more design-focused tool.

## Virtual Staging AI pricing

You can try an upload for free with no sign-up or credit card. As of October 2026, paid plans on yearly billing are Basic at $16 per month for 6 photos, Standard at $19 per month for 20 photos, Professional at $39 per month for 60 photos and Enterprise at $79 per month for 150 photos. Yearly billing is advertised as up to 50 percent off monthly rates. All plans include unlimited renders, furniture removal and no watermark, and higher tiers add image storage, a success manager and API access.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Each plan caps how many new photos you can stage per month
- Virtually staged photos should be labeled as such in listings to avoid misleading buyers
- Results depend on photo quality; dark or distorted wide-angle shots stage less convincingly
- It stages rooms but does not handle renovations like new flooring or wall changes in detail

## Virtual Staging AI vs alternatives

REimagineHome is a better fit if you want broader AI interior and exterior redesign, such as changing finishes or landscaping, not just adding furniture. Curbora bundles staging with photo enhancement, decluttering and day-to-dusk conversion, and keeps originals attached for disclosure. ImovPro.ai goes further by turning listing photos into narrated videos and listing copy. Virtual Staging AI wins when you want fast, low-cost furniture staging with unlimited regenerations at a predictable monthly price.

## Tips for getting started with Virtual Staging AI

Shoot rooms from a corner at eye level with even lighting, which gives the AI clearer floor and wall lines to work with. Use furniture removal on occupied homes before staging rather than staging over existing pieces. Generate several versions and pick the one that best fits the home's price point and buyer profile. Keep the original photo in the listing next to the staged one.

## Virtual Staging AI FAQ

Q: Is Virtual Staging AI free?
A: You can try Virtual Staging AI with a free upload and no sign-up. Paid plans start at $16 per month on yearly billing for 6 photos.

Q: What is Virtual Staging AI used for?
A: Virtual Staging AI is used by real estate agents and photographers to add furniture to empty room photos for listings and marketing.

Q: Is virtual staging allowed on MLS listings?
A: Generally yes, but most MLS rules require virtually staged photos to be clearly disclosed, so check your local MLS policy before publishing.

Q: What is the best alternative to Virtual Staging AI?
A: REimagineHome is a strong alternative for broader AI redesigns, and Curbora suits agents who also want photo enhancement and decluttering.

Cal AI is a calorie tracking app that estimates calories and macros from a photo of your food for people who want to lose weight, gain muscle or simply eat with more awareness. The pitch is speed: instead of searching a food database and guessing grams, you take a picture and adjust the result. It became one of the most downloaded nutrition apps of the last two years largely because that photo-first flow removes the main reason people abandon food diaries.

## What is Cal AI used for?

Most people use Cal AI as a daily food log with a calorie and macro goal. The app asks about your height, weight, activity and target during onboarding, sets a daily budget, and then tracks what you eat against it.

- Snapping a photo of a meal to get estimated calories, protein, carbs and fat
- Using the phone depth sensor, where available, to judge portion volume
- Scanning packaged food barcodes for label-accurate numbers
- Typing a short description when a photo is impractical, such as a coffee order
- Syncing steps and workouts from Apple Health or Google Fit
- Reviewing streaks and weekly progress toward a weight goal

## Who Cal AI is best for

Cal AI suits people who have tried MyFitnessPal style logging and gave up because it was tedious, and who are happy with a reasonable estimate rather than lab precision. It works well for home-cooked plates and restaurant meals where you would otherwise guess. People managing a medical condition such as diabetes, or anyone with a history of disordered eating, should talk to a clinician or dietitian before relying on any calorie app, and should treat Cal AI numbers as approximate.

## Cal AI pricing

Cal AI is free to download and starts with a 3-day free trial that turns into a paid subscription. The website does not publish a price list. As of October 2026 the App Store listing shows several subscription options, with in-app prices ranging from $2.99 to $29.99 depending on the plan and offer, and the exact price you see appears after onboarding inside the app. There is no permanent free tier and no team or enterprise plan. Check the paywall in the app before the trial ends so you know what you will be charged.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Photo estimates struggle with cooking oil, dressings, sauces and mixed dishes such as stews
- Portion size is still an estimate, so totals can drift if you never correct them
- Pricing is shown only inside the app, which makes comparison shopping harder
- It is a consumer wellness tool, not medical nutrition therapy

## Cal AI vs alternatives

123 Cal covers the same photo-to-macros job and shows a likely range for each estimate, which is useful if you want to see how uncertain a reading is. LifeOS AI is the better choice if food is only one part of what you want to track alongside habits, goals and finances. ChatGPT can estimate the calories in a meal photo too, but it does not keep a running daily log, targets or streaks unless you build that yourself. Cal AI wins when you want a dedicated mobile food diary with barcode scanning and activity sync that you will open several times a day.

## Tips for getting started with Cal AI

Take photos from directly above the plate in good light and keep the whole portion in frame, since cut-off edges lead to low estimates. After each scan, open the result and add anything the camera cannot see, such as butter in the pan or sugar in a drink. Use barcode scanning for anything packaged, because label data beats a visual guess. Finally, weigh a few common meals once with a kitchen scale and compare them with the app so you learn where it tends to over or under count.

## Cal AI FAQ

Q: Is Cal AI free?
A: No. Cal AI offers a 3-day free trial, after which a paid subscription is required to keep logging meals with the photo scanner.

Q: How accurate is Cal AI?
A: Cal AI gives estimates, not exact measurements. Simple plated foods tend to work well, while sauces, oils and mixed dishes need manual correction for reliable totals.

Q: Does Cal AI work on Android?
A: Yes. Cal AI is available on both the Apple App Store and Google Play, and it connects to Apple Health or Google Fit for activity data.

Q: What is the best alternative to Cal AI?
A: 123 Cal is the closest alternative for photo-based macro logging, while ChatGPT can estimate a single meal photo if you do not need a daily food diary.

## What is Fitbod used for?

Fitbod replaces the notebook or spreadsheet many lifters use, and also the guesswork about what to do next. You open the app, get a workout, and log sets as you go.

- Generating a full gym or home session based on muscle recovery and goals
- Applying progressive overload by suggesting slightly heavier weights or more reps over time
- Learning exercises from demo videos and form cues in a library of more than 1,000 moves

- Syncing workouts with Apple Health, Apple Watch, Strava and Fitbit

Fitbod fits beginners who feel lost in a gym, intermediate lifters who have stalled on random programs, and people training at home with dumbbells or bands. It is less useful for athletes following a coach's periodized plan, powerlifters peaking for a meet, or anyone whose main training is running, cycling or team sport, since the app is built specifically for resistance training.

- No free plan after the trial ends

Fitbod wins for people who want the app to decide the next session automatically and keep weights moving up week after week.

## Tips for getting started with Fitbod

Set your equipment list carefully, including bar weight and the dumbbell increments your gym actually has, because the plan depends on it. Log your first few sessions honestly, even if the weights feel light, so the algorithm can calibrate your strength. Use the exercise swap when something hurts rather than skipping the move, which keeps the muscle balance intact. If you train at more than one location, create a separate gym profile for each.

## Fitbod FAQ

Q: Is Fitbod free?

Q: Does Fitbod work at home without a gym?

name: Ash
tagline: AI built for mental health conversations, by voice or text, that remembers your story
description: Ash is a mental health support app from Slingshot AI that lets you talk or text with an AI built for emotional wellbeing, with memory, weekly insights and guided next steps.
longDescription: Ash is an emotional support app for iOS and Android built by Slingshot AI. Rather than adapting a general chatbot, the company trained a model specifically on psychology using proprietary expert data, and specialists in emotional wellbeing help design how it responds. You can talk to Ash like a phone call or text it at any hour. It remembers your stories, preferences and progress so conversations pick up where they left off, and weekly insights connect current struggles with patterns from earlier chats. Ash can follow your agenda or suggest a next step for everyday challenges such as stress, relationships, work and sleep. The company states clearly that Ash is not designed for use in a crisis and points users to crisis lines. It launched publicly in 2025 and offers paid unlimited access inside the app.
features: Voice or text conversations at any hour
Memory of past conversations and progress
Weekly insights that link patterns over time
Model trained specifically for psychology
pros: Purpose-built for emotional conversations rather than general chat
Voice mode feels closer to talking than typing
Clear crisis disclaimer and signposting
cons: Not suitable for crisis or severe mental illness
Pricing for unlimited access is only shown in the app
moreContext:
Ash is an AI mental health app that offers voice and text conversations for people working through everyday emotional challenges such as stress, relationships, work pressure and low mood. It is made by Slingshot AI, which trained its own model on psychology data instead of wrapping a general assistant, and it is designed with input from mental health specialists. Ash is a support tool, not a licensed therapist, and the company says plainly that it is not meant for crisis situations.

## What is Ash used for?

People use Ash to talk things out when a friend or professional is not available, and to notice patterns in how they think and react over time.

- Talking out loud with Ash like a phone call, or texting it for private guidance
- Picking up conversations where they left off, since Ash remembers past chats
- Getting weekly insights that connect a current issue with something from months earlier
- Following suggested next steps when you are not sure where to start
- Reflecting on sleep, stress, conflict at home or work worries between therapy sessions

## Who Ash is best for

Ash suits adults who want a judgment-free space to process feelings, people on a waiting list for therapy who want structured support in the meantime, and people in therapy who want help reflecting between sessions. It is not suitable for anyone in crisis, at risk of self-harm, or living with severe mental illness, who should contact emergency services, a crisis line or a licensed clinician.

## Ash pricing

Ash was free to use when it launched publicly in 2025. As of October 2026 the App Store listing shows in-app purchases labeled unlimited access, with prices ranging from $9.99 to $169.99 depending on the billing period and offer, which suggests paid plans for heavier use. The website does not publish a pricing page, so check the subscription screen in the app for what is free and what costs money in your region.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Not a crisis service and not a substitute for a licensed therapist or psychiatrist
- Plan details and limits are only visible inside the app
- Sharing deeply personal information with any app carries privacy risk, so review the consumer health data notice
- AI can misread context, so treat its suggestions as prompts for reflection, not instructions

## Ash vs alternatives

Healing Journey offers chats with several AI therapist personas focused on topics like anxiety and habits, which some people like for variety. Iris works over iMessage and RCS, so it suits people who prefer support inside their normal texting app. Pi is a free, warm general conversational AI that is good for casual talking but is not built specifically for mental health. Maia is the better choice for couples who want a shared space to work through conflict. Ash stands out for its psychology-specific model, voice mode and long-term memory.

## Tips for getting started with Ash

Tell Ash in the first conversation what you want from it, such as handling work stress or preparing for hard conversations, so its guidance has a direction. Try voice mode at least once, since many users find speaking easier than typing about feelings. Read the weekly insight and push back if it gets something wrong, which helps it adjust. Save local crisis numbers in your phone separately, because Ash is not an emergency resource.

## Ash FAQ

Q: Is Ash free?
A: Ash launched as a free app, and as of October 2026 the App Store also lists paid unlimited access plans from $9.99, so check the app for current limits.

Q: Is Ash a replacement for therapy?
A: No. Ash is an AI support tool for everyday emotional challenges. It is not a licensed therapist and is not designed for crises or severe mental illness.

Q: Who makes the Ash app?
A: Ash is made by Slingshot AI, a company that trained its own psychology-focused AI model and launched Ash publicly in July 2025.

Q: What is the best alternative to Ash?
A: Healing Journey is a close alternative with AI therapist personas, while Iris suits people who want support through iMessage or RCS text messages.

name: Wysa
tagline: Anonymous AI wellbeing chat with evidence-based exercises and optional human coaching
description: Wysa is an AI mental wellbeing app that offers anonymous, around-the-clock conversations, guides users to evidence-based exercises, and adds optional human coaching for individuals, employers and health systems.
longDescription: Wysa is a conversational AI for emotional wellbeing used by individuals and by employers, insurers and health services. Its chatbot uses reflective dialogue to understand how you feel and then suggests techniques such as CBT-style exercises, mindfulness, guided journaling and grounding tools. It is anonymous, so you can start without sharing personal details, and an always-visible SOS button links to crisis resources. Talking to the AI is free, while a premium version adds a larger tool library, and some regions offer paid text or video coaching with human wellbeing professionals. Wysa is backed by peer-reviewed research and received an FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for an AI conversational agent for chronic pain with related depression and anxiety. The app is for people aged 13 and over and is not a crisis service or a substitute for medical advice.
features: Anonymous AI chat available around the clock
CBT, mindfulness and journaling exercises
SOS button and distress detection
Optional human coaching in some regions
pros: Free AI conversations with no sign-up details required
Peer-reviewed research behind the approach
Strong safety features and clear scope
cons: Premium tools and coaching cost extra
Not suitable for crisis or severe and enduring conditions
moreContext:
Wysa is an AI mental wellbeing app that provides anonymous, always-available conversations and evidence-based self-help exercises for individuals, employees and patients. It is one of the longest-running apps in the category and stands out for its clinical approach: the AI is built on clinically validated conversation logic, monitored for safety, and backed by peer-reviewed studies. Wysa is clear that it supports wellbeing and does not diagnose or provide medical advice.

## What is Wysa used for?

Wysa helps people manage stress, worry and low mood in the moment and build coping skills over time. Many users reach it through an employer, school, insurer or health service, while others download it directly.

- Talking through feelings with an anonymous AI at any hour
- Practicing CBT-style reframing, breathing, grounding and mindfulness exercises
- Using guided journaling prompts suggested by the conversation
- Reaching crisis helplines quickly through an always-visible SOS button
- Booking text or video sessions with a human wellbeing professional in supported regions
- Supporting people between appointments or while they wait for care

## Who Wysa is best for

Wysa suits people who want private, stigma-free support for everyday stress and anxiety, and organizations that want a safe, evidence-based wellbeing tool for staff or patients. It is intended for people aged 13 and over. Wysa states that it is not a crisis service and is not suitable for people with severe and enduring mental health problems, who should work with clinicians directly.

## Wysa pricing

Talking to the Wysa AI is free, including the tools offered inside conversations. A premium subscription unlocks a much wider tool library you can browse directly, and human coaching costs extra in some locations. As of October 2026 the App Store lists Wysa Premium at $19.99 per month and annual options from $74.99, plus separate guided support plans with a human professional. People who get Wysa through an employer, school or insurer receive premium access at no cost. Organizations should book a demo for enterprise pricing.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Not a crisis service and not a replacement for professional diagnosis or treatment
- The richest tool library and human coaching are paid
- Scripted structure can feel less free-flowing than general chatbots
- Organizational deployments may share anonymized, population-level trends with the sponsor

## Wysa vs alternatives

Healing Journey offers open-ended chats with AI therapist personas, which feels more conversational but has less published research behind it. Iris works over text message, which suits people who want support inside their usual messaging app. Pi is a free, friendly general conversational AI that is good for talking things through but is not designed around clinical techniques. Docus AI is the better tool when your question is about physical symptoms or lab results rather than emotional wellbeing. Wysa wins on evidence, safety features and organizational deployment.

## Tips for getting started with Wysa

Start by describing a specific situation, such as trouble sleeping before a presentation, so Wysa can suggest a matching exercise. Try a few different tools in the first week and note which ones actually help. Check whether your employer, university or insurer offers Wysa, since that unlocks premium for free. Learn where the SOS button is before you need it.

## Wysa FAQ

Q: Is Wysa free?
A: Yes. Chatting with the Wysa AI is free, and an optional premium subscription, listed at $19.99 per month in the App Store as of October 2026, adds more tools.

Q: Is Wysa FDA approved?
A: Wysa is not FDA approved as a general mental health treatment. It received an FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for an AI conversational agent for chronic pain with associated depression and anxiety.

Q: Is Wysa anonymous?
A: Yes. You can talk to the Wysa AI without providing personal information, and the company describes the experience as anonymous and stigma-free.

Q: What is the best alternative to Wysa?
A: Healing Journey is an alternative for open-ended AI therapist chats, and Iris suits people who want wellbeing support through text messages.

name: Mindtrip
tagline: AI travel assistant that plans, books and watches your trips for price drops and changes
description: Mindtrip is an AI travel assistant that learns your preferences, builds itineraries, explains flight, hotel and restaurant tradeoffs, and monitors trips for price drops, schedule changes and weather.
longDescription: Mindtrip is a travel planning assistant on the web and iPhone. You chat about where you want to go and how you like to travel, and it remembers those preferences so you do not repeat them on the next trip. It suggests flights, stays, restaurants and things to do, explains why each option fits, and keeps ideas, itineraries and bookings together in one trip. Once plans are set, Mindtrip watches for price drops, flight changes, restaurant availability and weather, and sends alerts and advice while you travel. You can also set up custom agents to track specific things you care about. Guides and recommendations from travelers and local experts add inspiration beyond the chat. The core planner is free to use after signing in with a Google or Apple account.
features: Chat-based itinerary planning with saved preferences
Explanations of tradeoffs between flights, stays and restaurants
Monitoring for price drops, flight changes and weather
Custom agents that track what you care about
pros: Free to plan without a subscription
Keeps planning and booking for a trip in one place
Alerts continue after you book, not only while planning
cons: Requires a Google or Apple sign-in to start
Recommendations still need checking against official sources
moreContext:
Mindtrip is an AI travel planner that builds itineraries, compares flights, hotels and restaurants, and keeps watch over your trip for travelers who want one assistant from first idea to the flight home. Its main difference from many itinerary generators is what happens after you plan: Mindtrip keeps monitoring prices, flight schedules, restaurant availability and weather, then nudges you when something changes. It also remembers how you like to travel, so the second trip starts smarter than the first.

## What is Mindtrip used for?

Mindtrip is used to turn a loose idea, such as a long weekend somewhere warm in March, into a concrete plan with bookings, and then to keep that plan on track.

- Chatting about destinations, budgets and travel style to get a day-by-day itinerary
- Comparing flights, stays and restaurants with explanations of why each option fits you
- Saving ideas, plans and bookings together in a single trip
- Getting alerts for price drops, flight changes, restaurant openings and weather
- Creating custom agents to track specific things, such as a hotel rate or a sold-out reservation
- Browsing guides and recommendations from travelers and local experts

## Who Mindtrip is best for

Mindtrip suits leisure travelers who plan their own trips and want help weighing options, couples and families coordinating a shared itinerary, and frequent travelers who like the idea of an assistant that remembers their preferences. Business travelers who must book through a corporate travel tool, and people who want a human agent to handle everything, will be better served elsewhere.

## Mindtrip pricing

Mindtrip's core travel assistant is free to use. As of October 2026 the pricing link on the site leads to a sign-in screen rather than a published price list, and no paid consumer tier was visible before signing in. You need a Google or Apple account to start. Bookings themselves are paid to the airline, hotel or provider at their normal prices. Businesses interested in partnerships or enterprise use should contact Mindtrip directly.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Account sign-in is required before you can try the planner
- AI suggestions can be out of date, so confirm opening hours, visa rules and prices with official sources
- Monitoring and alerts depend on the data sources Mindtrip connects to
- No public pricing page explains whether premium features may be added later

## Mindtrip vs alternatives

Layla pairs AI itineraries with real travel experts who refine and book hotels, flights and activities, so it is the better pick if you want human help. Wonderplan and Trip Planner AI are quick, simple itinerary drafters that work well when you only need a day-by-day plan to edit. Airial is strong if your inspiration starts from a TikTok or Reels link. GuideGeek lives inside messaging apps for quick questions on the go. Mindtrip wins when you want planning, booking and ongoing trip monitoring together, with memory of your preferences.

## Tips for getting started with Mindtrip

Spend the first conversation telling Mindtrip about your travel style in detail, such as budget range, pace, food preferences and seat or hotel must-haves, because it saves these for later trips. Ask it to explain tradeoffs between two or three options instead of asking for the single best one. Turn on alerts for flights and hotels as soon as you have candidates, so you catch price drops early. Before you travel, confirm entry requirements and reservations directly with the provider.

## Mindtrip FAQ

Q: Is Mindtrip free?
A: Yes. Mindtrip's AI travel assistant is free to use with a Google or Apple sign-in, and you pay providers directly for any flights, hotels or activities you book.

Q: Can Mindtrip book flights and hotels?
A: Yes. Mindtrip keeps bookings with your itinerary and lets you book directly or have the assistant handle details, then monitors the trip for changes.

Q: Does Mindtrip have an app?
A: Yes. Mindtrip works on the web at its official site and has an iPhone app, so plans sync between desktop and phone.

Q: What is the best alternative to Mindtrip?
A: Layla is a strong alternative if you want human travel experts to refine and book your trip, and Wonderplan suits people who only need a quick itinerary.

name: Alta
tagline: Free AI stylist and digital closet with avatar try-on, daily outfits and packing lists
description: Alta is a free AI stylist app that digitizes your wardrobe from photos, suggests daily outfits based on weather and plans, and lets you try looks on a virtual avatar of yourself.
longDescription: Alta is an AI stylist and digital closet built around the clothes you already own. You add items by snapping a photo, forwarding email receipts or picking from Alta's product database, and AI removes backgrounds, cleans up the image and tags fabric, fit and category. From there Alta recommends daily outfits based on your closet, schedule and local weather, and can build looks for a specific event or around one piece you want to wear. A virtual dressing room lets you try outfits on an avatar of you and plan them on a style calendar. For travel, it generates packing lists and lookbooks across multiple cities and climates. A wishlist tracks price drops, and wear stats show cost per wear. Alta was named a TIME Best Invention of 2025 and is free.
features: Digital closet from photos, receipts or a product database
Daily outfits based on weather and plans
Virtual avatar try-on and style calendar
Trip packing lists and travel lookbooks
pros: All features free at the time of writing
Clean product-style images of your own clothes
Cost-per-wear and most-worn stats encourage using what you own
cons: Cataloging a full wardrobe takes a few hours up front
Avatar try-on can take several attempts to look right
moreContext:
Alta is an AI stylist app that organizes your wardrobe into a digital closet and suggests outfits from clothes you already own for people who want to dress better without buying more. It combines closet cataloging, daily outfit recommendations, avatar try-on and trip planning in one free app, and was named a TIME Best Invention of 2025. Its focus on shopping your own closet first is what separates it from fashion apps built mainly to sell new clothes.

## What is Alta used for?

People use Alta to answer what to wear today, to plan outfits for events, and to pack for trips without overpacking.

- Building a digital closet by photographing clothes, forwarding receipts or searching the Alta database
- Getting daily outfit suggestions matched to the weather and your schedule
- Generating looks for a specific occasion, such as a job interview or date night
- Asking for outfits built around one piece you want to wear
- Trying outfits on a virtual avatar and saving them to a style calendar
- Creating packing lists and lookbooks for multi-city trips

## Who Alta is best for

Alta suits people with full closets who keep wearing the same few items, professionals who want a reliable work wardrobe plan, and frequent travelers who struggle with packing. It is also useful for anyone trying to shop more mindfully, thanks to cost-per-wear stats and a wishlist that tracks price drops. People with very small wardrobes, or who would rather get styling from a human, will get less out of it.

## Alta pricing

Alta is free to use. As of October 2026 the website states that the app is free, and the App Store listing shows no in-app purchases. There are no paid tiers or enterprise plans advertised. Because the product is young and AI image generation is costly to run, it is worth watching for a premium tier in future, but none was offered when checked.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Setting up a large wardrobe takes a few hours of photographing items
- The avatar may need several tries before it looks like you
- Outfit quality depends on how completely you catalog your closet
- Suggestions only cover clothes you have added, so gaps in the closet mean weaker outfits

## Alta vs alternatives

Aidrobe leans toward recommending new pieces based on your taste and country, with virtual try-on of items you might buy, so it is better if shopping is the goal. Klodsy also digitizes your closet and suggests combinations, and shows looks on your photo or a digital model. YouCam Makeup is the pick if you want to try on makeup, hairstyles and hair colors as well as outfits. Alta wins for people who want a free, closet-first stylist with weather-aware daily outfits and strong travel planning.

## Tips for getting started with Alta

Forward old order confirmation emails first, since that adds many items quickly without photographing them. Photograph the rest in batches on a plain surface with good light. Log what you actually wear for a couple of weeks so the stats and suggestions reflect real habits. Before your next trip, enter every city and activity along with your luggage size, and let Alta draft the packing list.

## Alta FAQ

Q: Is Alta free?
A: Yes. Alta is free to use, and as of October 2026 the app showed no in-app purchases or paid subscription.

Q: Can Alta show outfits on me?
A: Yes. Alta creates a virtual avatar of you in its dressing room, so you can try outfits on before wearing them and plan looks ahead on a calendar.

Q: How do I add clothes to Alta?
A: You can photograph items, forward email receipts, or search the Alta database, and the app cleans up images and tags each item automatically.

Q: What is the best alternative to Alta?
A: Klodsy is a close alternative for closet-based outfit suggestions, while Aidrobe suits people who want help choosing new clothes to buy.

name: Acloset
tagline: AI closet app that catalogs clothes, picks daily outfits and tries looks on your avatar
description: Acloset is an AI fashion assistant that turns photos and online orders into a digital closet, recommends outfits for the weather and your plans, and offers avatar-based virtual try-on.
longDescription: Acloset is a smart closet app from Looko Inc. that helps you see and use everything you own. You can photograph clothes one after another, upload a mirror selfie and let AI detect each item, or import past purchases from online stores and order emails through Gmail or forwarding. The AI stylist picks outfits for the weather and your plans for today or the coming week, completes a look around a piece you have already chosen, and analyzes your colors and body type. Virtual try-on creates an avatar from your photo so you can see your own clothes, wishlist items or suggested outfits on you. Trip packing uses real weather data, widgets show today's pick, and style stats reveal what you wear and what sits unused. A free version is available, with paid tiers for more features.
features: Batch photo and mirror selfie item detection
Import purchases from online stores and order emails
Weather-aware outfit picks for the week
Avatar virtual try-on and color analysis
pros: Fast ways to add a whole wardrobe
Available in many languages
Low-cost entry tier
cons: Several tiers and an in-app currency make pricing confusing
Try-on quality depends on the photo you supply
moreContext:
Acloset is an AI wardrobe app that organizes your clothes into a digital closet and recommends outfits for people who own plenty but still feel they have nothing to wear. It has been around since 2021, says it is trusted by 8 million users, and was a Google Play Editor's Pick. Its strengths are the many ways it gets clothes into the app quickly, from mirror selfies to imported online orders, and its mix of styling, try-on and wear analytics.

## What is Acloset used for?

Acloset is used to catalog a wardrobe, plan daily outfits, and make smarter buying decisions.

- Photographing many items in a row and adding them at once
- Uploading a mirror selfie and letting AI detect each item you are wearing
- Importing past purchases from online stores or from order emails via Gmail or forwarding
- Getting outfit picks for today or any day in the coming week based on weather and plans
- Completing a look around one item, and analyzing personal colors and body type
- Trying clothes on an AI avatar created from your photo, and packing for trips with weather data

## Who Acloset is best for

Acloset suits people with large or growing wardrobes, fashion fans who want to track what they wear, and shoppers trying to avoid buying duplicates. Its wide language support makes it a good fit outside English-speaking markets. People with minimal wardrobes or no interest in logging outfits may not use it enough to justify a paid tier.

## Acloset pricing

Acloset is free to download with a free version of the core closet. As of October 2026 the App Store lists paid tiers starting with Basic at $3.99 per month or $27.99 per year, Premium at $9.99 per month or $59.99 per year, and Expert at $24.99 per month or $147.99 per year. The app also sells an in-app currency called beans in packs from $1.99, used for features such as AI generation. There is no business plan for consumers. Check the app for which features each tier unlocks.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Multiple tiers plus beans make the true cost of AI features harder to judge
- Imported purchases may need manual cleanup for color and category
- Virtual try-on is an approximation and may not reflect real fit
- Most value comes after the closet is fully cataloged, which takes time

## Acloset vs alternatives

Aidrobe is the better choice if you mainly want suggestions for new clothes to buy based on your taste and country. Klodsy is a close rival for digitizing a closet and seeing combinations on your own photo or a model. YouCam Makeup covers makeup, hair and outfit try-on in one app, so it suits people focused on overall looks rather than closet management. Acloset wins on the variety of import methods, multi-language support and a low entry price for paid features.

## Tips for getting started with Acloset

Start by importing past online orders, which can add dozens of items in minutes. Use the mirror selfie feature for outfits you already wear often, so your favorites are captured first. Log what you wear daily for two weeks to make the style stats meaningful. Before buying a new item, add it to the wishlist and try it on your avatar with clothes you own to see whether it really fills a gap.

## Acloset FAQ

Q: Is Acloset free?
A: Yes. Acloset has a free version, and paid tiers start at $3.99 per month for Basic in the App Store as of October 2026.

Q: Can Acloset import clothes from online stores?
A: Yes. Acloset can import past purchases from many online stores and from order emails through Gmail or email forwarding, so you do not need to photograph everything.

Q: Does Acloset have virtual try-on?
A: Yes. Acloset creates an AI avatar from your photo so you can try on your own clothes, wishlist items or suggested outfits.

Q: What is the best alternative to Acloset?
A: Klodsy is a close alternative for closet-based outfit planning, and Aidrobe suits people who want AI help choosing new clothes to buy.

name: Doji
tagline: Try on designer fashion with a photorealistic AI likeness of yourself, then shop the look
description: Doji is a free iPhone app that builds a photorealistic AI likeness from your photos so you can try on designer clothes, remix looks, save a wishlist and shop items directly.
longDescription: Doji is a virtual try-on and social shopping app for iPhone from Doji Labs. You upload a few photos and the app creates a photorealistic AI likeness of you, which becomes your model for trying on clothes. You can try on personalized picks, add products from anywhere online, remix looks other people have made, or build outfits from scratch. A digital closet holds clothes you already own, and a wishlist saves pieces you are considering, with recommendations based on your style. Items can be bought directly in the app, and a browser extension lets you try on products while browsing other fashion sites. Social features let you follow friends, tastemakers and brands, and share your looks. Doji is free and requires iOS 18 or later.
features: Photorealistic AI likeness built from your photos
Try on items from Doji or anywhere online
Browser extension for try-on while shopping
Digital closet, wishlist and social feed
pros: Free with no in-app purchases listed
Realistic try-on of designer pieces before buying
Works with products from other fashion sites
cons: iPhone only and needs iOS 18 or later
Try-on images show appearance, not true fit or sizing
moreContext:
Doji is a virtual try-on app that creates a photorealistic AI version of you so you can see how designer clothes look before you buy them, aimed at fashion-curious shoppers who want to experiment. Instead of tapping through flat product photos, you browse looks on your own likeness, remix outfits from the community and shop the pieces. It mixes try-on, styling and a social feed, with a playful tone that encourages trying styles you would not normally pick.

## What is Doji used for?

Doji is used to preview clothes on yourself, explore new styles and save or buy items you like.

- Creating a realistic AI likeness from a few uploaded photos
- Trying on personalized picks and designer pieces on that likeness
- Adding products from anywhere online and trying them on
- Remixing other people's looks or building outfits from scratch
- Keeping a digital closet of clothes you own and a wishlist of items to consider
- Using a browser extension to try on items while shopping other fashion websites

## Who Doji is best for

Doji suits fashion fans, online shoppers who are tired of guessing how a piece will look, and people who enjoy sharing outfits with friends. It is a good fit for trying bolder styles at no cost. People who mainly need fit and sizing guidance, Android users, and those who prefer not to upload photos of themselves to build an AI likeness should look elsewhere.

## Doji pricing

Doji is free. As of October 2026 the App Store lists the app as free with no in-app purchases shown, and the website does not advertise paid plans. Items you buy through the app are paid at the retailer's price. There is no business or brand plan published on the site, so brands interested in partnering should contact the team through the address on the website.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- iPhone only, requiring iOS 18 or later
- Try-on shows how a garment looks on your likeness, not how it will actually fit
- Building a likeness requires uploading personal photos, so review the privacy policy
- The social feed and shopping focus may distract people who only want closet organization

## Doji vs alternatives

Aidrobe also offers virtual try-on and suggests clothing based on your taste and country, and works well for people who want recommendations first. Klodsy is the better pick if your priority is digitizing your existing closet and getting outfit combinations from it. YouCam Makeup covers makeup, hair color and hairstyles as well as outfits, so it suits people who want to test a complete look. Doji wins for realistic designer try-on on your own likeness, a browser extension for shopping anywhere, and a social layer for sharing looks.

## Tips for getting started with Doji

Upload clear, well-lit photos from a few angles when creating your likeness, since better inputs produce more realistic try-ons. Install the browser extension so you can try on items from the stores you already shop. Add a handful of clothes you own to the closet, then mix them with wishlist pieces to see whether a new item works with your wardrobe. Always check the retailer's size guide before buying, because try-on does not measure fit.

## Doji FAQ

Q: Is Doji free?
A: Yes. Doji is free on the App Store, and as of October 2026 no in-app purchases or subscriptions were listed.

Q: How does Doji virtual try-on work?
A: Doji builds a photorealistic AI likeness from a few photos you upload, then renders clothes from its catalog or other websites on that likeness.

Q: Is Doji available on Android?
A: No. Doji is an iPhone app that requires iOS 18 or later, though a browser extension supports try-on while shopping on fashion websites.

Q: What is the best alternative to Doji?
A: Aidrobe is a close alternative for virtual try-on with clothing suggestions, and Klodsy suits people who want outfits built from their existing closet.

name: Friends & Fables
tagline: AI game master for D&D style tabletop campaigns with 5e combat, maps and multiplayer
description: Friends & Fables is an AI tabletop RPG platform where an AI game master named Franz runs D&D 5e inspired campaigns, with world-building tools, tactical combat and parties of up to six.
longDescription: Friends & Fables is a text-based roleplaying platform inspired by Dungeons and Dragons. Its AI game master, Franz, narrates campaigns, adapts to player choices and keeps long-term memories of what happened. Combat is tactical and turn-based on battlemaps using D&D 5e rules, with spells, abilities and monsters drawn from the SRD 5.1. World builders get a toolkit for maps, characters, quests, one-shots and lore, and can upload existing lore for the AI to weave into play. Parties of up to six can adventure together, and friends can join a subscriber's campaign for free. Text-to-speech narration with character voices and image generation for characters, items and locations add atmosphere. A free plan allows 25 game master turns per day, and paid plans remove the limit. The platform says it has more than 100,000 players.

Turn-based 5e combat on battlemaps
Map, character, quest and lore building tools
Multiplayer parties of up to six players
pros: Real rules-based combat instead of freeform text only
Friends can join a paid campaign for free

moreContext:
Friends & Fables is an AI tabletop RPG platform where an AI game master runs Dungeons and Dragons style campaigns for solo players and groups of friends. The game master, called Franz, narrates the story, voices characters and adapts to your choices, while the platform handles 5e-style rules, battlemaps and inventory. What sets it apart from pure text adventure apps is the structure: tactical turn-based combat, a travel system and a full world-building toolkit sit on top of the storytelling.

## What is Friends & Fables used for?

Friends & Fables is used for playing tabletop-style campaigns without needing a human dungeon master, and for building worlds that others can play.

- Running solo or group campaigns with an AI game master that remembers past sessions
- Fighting turn-based battles on battlemaps using D&D 5e rules, spells and monsters
- Building worlds with map makers, character generators, quests and one-shot adventures
- Uploading your own lore so the AI weaves it into campaigns
- Playing with up to six people in a party
- Hearing narration and character voices through text-to-speech, and generating images of characters and places

## Who Friends & Fables is best for

Friends & Fables suits D&D fans who cannot find a regular game master, groups whose schedules make in-person sessions hard, and world builders who want their settings to come alive. It is also a gentle entry point for newcomers curious about tabletop RPGs. Players who want purely freeform storytelling without rules, or who prefer visual video games, may find the text and dice structure slow.

## Friends & Fables pricing

Friends & Fables has a free plan with up to 25 game master turns per day, long-term memories, unlimited campaign slots and three-player campaigns. As of October 2026 the paid plans are Starter at $19.95 per month with unlimited standard turns, text-to-speech, four-player campaigns and 100 bonus monthly credits; Pro at $29.95 per month with five-player campaigns and 300 credits; and Legend at $39.95 per month with six-player campaigns and 600 credits. Yearly billing gives two months free. Friends can play in a subscriber's campaign at no cost.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- The free tier's 25 turns per day can run out quickly in an active session
- It is an independent product and not affiliated with Dungeons and Dragons or Wizards of the Coast
- The AI can still lose track of details in very long campaigns
- Text-based play is slower than a visual video game

## Friends & Fables vs alternatives

AI Dungeon is the original AI text adventure and is better for freeform storytelling in any genre without rules mechanics. Hidden Door offers AI-narrated stories in licensed worlds such as Sherlock Holmes and Oz, which suits players who prefer familiar settings. RPGGO and Teasa focus on creator-built adventures and AI characters you can chat with. Friends & Fables wins for players who want an actual D&D-style experience with 5e combat, battlemaps and a party of friends.

## Tips for getting started with Friends & Fables

Start with a featured public world to learn how Franz handles combat and pacing before building your own. Write clear custom instructions about tone, difficulty and how much the game master should narrate versus ask you. If you play in a group, have one person subscribe and invite friends, since they can join for free. When building a world, upload key lore early so the AI keeps names and history consistent.

## Friends & Fables FAQ

Q: Is Friends & Fables free?
A: Yes. Friends & Fables has a free plan with 25 game master turns per day, and paid plans start at $19.95 per month for unlimited standard turns.

Q: Does Friends & Fables use real D&D rules?
A: Yes. Combat follows D&D 5e rules using material from the System Reference Document 5.1, though the platform is not affiliated with Wizards of the Coast.

Q: Can I play Friends & Fables with friends?
A: Yes. Campaigns support parties of up to six players depending on the plan, and friends can join a subscriber's campaign for free.

Q: What is the best alternative to Friends & Fables?
A: AI Dungeon is the best alternative for freeform AI storytelling, while Hidden Door suits players who want stories set in well-known fictional worlds.

As of October 2026 the App Store lists PictureThis Pro at several price points, most often $39.99, plus lower-priced options and a Family Plan at $49.99. New subscriptions are often offered with a free trial that renews automatically, so set a reminder if you only want to test it. There is no business plan for consumers.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- The free tier is limited, and upgrade screens appear often
- Trials can roll into an annual charge if you forget to cancel
- Identification accuracy drops with blurry photos, seedlings or unusual cultivars
- Never rely on any app alone to decide whether a plant is edible

## PictureThis vs alternatives

Google Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude can all identify a plant from an uploaded photo and answer follow-up questions about care in plain language, which is enough for occasional use at no extra cost. They do not provide a dedicated plant library, toxicity lists by region or a saved collection of your own plants. PictureThis is the better choice for frequent identification, regular care guidance and diagnosis in an app built specifically for plants.

## Tips for getting started with PictureThis

Photograph a single leaf, flower or the whole plant in good light, filling the frame, and take more than one shot if the first result looks uncertain. For diagnosis, include both healthy and damaged leaves so the comparison is clear. Check the toxicity section before bringing a new plant home if you have pets or toddlers. If you start a Pro trial, cancel in your app store settings before it renews unless you plan to keep it.

## PictureThis FAQ

Q: Is PictureThis free?
A: Partly. PictureThis is free to download with limited free identifications, and a Pro subscription, most often listed at $39.99 in the App Store, unlocks unlimited use.

Q: How accurate is PictureThis?
A: PictureThis is accurate for most common plants in clear photos, but results can be wrong for blurry images, young seedlings or rare varieties.

Q: Can PictureThis tell if a plant is toxic to pets?
A: Yes. PictureThis shows toxicity information for many plants, including whether they are harmful to cats, dogs or children.

Q: What is the best alternative to PictureThis?
A: Google Gemini is a good free alternative for occasional plant identification from a photo, while ChatGPT can also answer care questions about a plant you upload.

name: Amp
tagline: Coding agent for the terminal that can keep working on remote machines after you log off
description: Amp is an AI coding agent you run from the terminal or on remote machines called orbs, where agents keep coding, testing and previewing changes after you close your laptop.
longDescription: Amp is a coding agent built for developers who want to hand off real tasks rather than chat about code. You install the CLI and run it inside a repository, where it reads files, runs commands and edits code. Its distinctive piece is orbs: remote machines that get a fresh copy of your code, plugins and tools for each thread, so an agent can keep working unattended. Portals let you run the app inside an orb and try the agent's changes with live reload. Automations can wake agents on a schedule or from webhooks such as a new Linear issue, and threads can be shared with teammates. A free Hobby tier lets you bring your own model subscriptions or keys, and a $20 monthly Individual plan adds hosted orb time.

Orbs: remote machines where agents run unattended

Scheduled and webhook-triggered automations
pros: Free tier works with your existing ChatGPT, Claude or API keys
Agents keep running after you close your laptop
Team features such as shared billing and SSO add no extra charge
cons: Hosted orb time is pay-as-you-go on the free tier
Built around the terminal, so developers who want a visual IDE may prefer an editor-based tool
moreContext:
Amp is an AI coding agent that writes, runs and tests code from your terminal or on remote machines for developers who want to delegate whole tasks. Where many assistants live inside an editor and wait for you, Amp is built around long-running threads: you describe the work, and the agent can keep going on a remote machine after you shut your laptop. That remote layer, which Amp calls orbs, is the main thing that sets it apart from a plain command line agent.

## What is Amp used for?

Developers use Amp to hand off feature work, bug fixes and refactors that take more than a few prompts. The CLI runs locally against your files and tools, and a headless mode covers servers and CI runners.

- Running the agent in a local repository to read code, edit files and execute shell commands
- Starting threads on orbs, remote machines that get a fresh copy of your code, plugins and tools for each task
- Opening a portal to run the app inside an orb and check the agent's changes with live reload
- Triggering agents on a schedule or from webhooks, for example when a new Linear issue is filed
- Sharing threads with teammates, working in a shared terminal, and catching up with a Recap summary after time away

## Who Amp is best for

Amp suits experienced engineers who are comfortable in the terminal and want an agent that can work in parallel with them, plus small teams that want to queue up issues and review the results later. If you mainly want inline autocomplete while you type, or you prefer a graphical editor with chat in a side panel, an IDE-based assistant will feel more natural.

## Amp pricing

As of October 2026, Amp's pricing page lists a free Hobby tier. It lets you use tokens from your own ChatGPT, Claude or other subscriptions or bring your own API keys, includes unlimited self-hosted orbs, and charges pay-as-you-go for orbs that Amp hosts. The Individual plan costs $20 per month and adds 45,000 minutes of hosted orb time, custom domains for portals and the same no-fee token access. Team features such as shared billing, pooled credits, thread sharing, permissions and SAML or OIDC single sign-on come at no extra charge, with members on any tier. Enterprise pricing is custom and adds SCIM, audit logs, IP allowlisting, spend limits and regional endpoints.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Model costs still exist: on the free tier you pay through your own subscriptions or keys, and hosted orb time is metered
- The workflow is terminal-first, which has a learning curve for developers used to an editor sidebar
- Amp-hosted orbs mean your code runs on Amp's machines unless you self-host them

## Amp vs alternatives

Claude Code is the closest comparison: a terminal agent from Anthropic that is tightly tuned to Claude models and is a good fit if your team already pays for Claude. OpenAI Codex is the better pick if you live in the ChatGPT ecosystem and want cloud tasks launched from the ChatGPT interface. Cursor wins for developers who want an AI-first editor with autocomplete and visual diffs rather than a command line. OpenCode is a free, open-source terminal agent for people who want full control over models and hosting. Choose Amp when remote machines, live previews and automated triggers matter more than staying inside one editor.

## Tips for getting started with Amp

Start locally in a small repository so you can watch how the agent reads files and runs commands before you trust it with remote work. Link an existing model subscription or API key first, since the free tier does not charge token fees on top of it. When you try orbs, give each thread a narrow, testable goal and open a portal to check the result in a running app.

## Amp FAQ

Q: Is Amp free?
A: Yes, Amp has a free Hobby tier where you use your own model subscriptions or API keys and pay as you go for Amp-hosted orbs. The Individual plan is $20 per month as of October 2026.

Q: Can I use my ChatGPT or Claude subscription with Amp?
A: Yes. Amp's pricing page says you can use tokens from your own ChatGPT, Claude or other subscriptions, or bring your own API keys, without Amp token fees.

Q: What is the best alternative to Amp?
A: Claude Code is the closest terminal-based alternative, OpenAI Codex suits ChatGPT users, and Cursor is better if you prefer working inside an AI code editor.

Google Antigravity is an agentic development platform from Google that lets developers plan, write and test software by directing AI agents instead of typing every line. It goes beyond a single editor: there is a desktop app for managing several agents at once, a full IDE, a command line tool and an SDK. For individual developers it is available at no charge, which makes it one of the easiest ways to try an agent-first workflow on your own projects.

## What is Google Antigravity used for?

Antigravity is used for building and maintaining software with agents that can read a codebase, propose changes, run commands and check their own work. Google pitches it at everyone from enterprise engineers to hobbyists.

- Running multiple local agents in parallel from the Antigravity App and grouping their conversations into projects across workspaces
- Editing code in the Antigravity IDE with an agent manager, artifacts and codebase context
- Using browser-in-the-loop agents to click through and test frontend changes
- Running autonomous agents, shell commands and background subagents from the Antigravity CLI
- Prototyping custom agents and running evaluations with the Python-based Antigravity SDK

## Who Google Antigravity is best for

It fits individual developers and students who want a capable agentic IDE without paying, teams already on Google Cloud or Gemini Enterprise, and frontend developers who like agents that can verify UI changes in a browser. Former Gemini CLI users on the unpaid tier are effectively pointed here, since the Gemini CLI site says it was replaced by the Antigravity CLI for that tier in June 2026. Developers who want to pick from many third-party models, or who need a tool that runs fully offline, should look elsewhere.

## Google Antigravity pricing

As of October 2026, the pricing page lists an Individuals tier at $0 per month with access to a range of agent models, unlimited Tab completions and Command requests, and basic weekly rate limits. Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra subscribers get progressively higher rate limits plus a flexible AI credit pool, though the page does not print those subscription prices. For organizations, Antigravity is sold through Google Cloud: Gemini Enterprise Standard and Plus seats start at $30 per user per month, a pay-as-you-go option has no seat fee, and API use is billed by consumption. Business plans add Google Cloud terms, spend caps and central admin controls.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- The free tier's weekly limits are not published as numbers, so heavy users may hit them without warning
- Model choice centers on Google's own Gemini models
- Enterprise use requires going through Google Cloud billing and admin setup

## Google Antigravity vs alternatives

Cursor is the most popular AI code editor and offers broader model choice, so it is the safer pick if you want to switch between providers. Devin Desktop, formerly Windsurf, is a close match for developers who want an agentic editor from a company focused only on coding tools. Kiro, from AWS, is better if you like spec-driven development where requirements and design docs come first. GitHub Copilot makes sense for teams that want AI inside their existing editor and GitHub workflow. Google Antigravity wins on price for individuals and on running several agents side by side from one desktop app.

## Tips for getting started with Google Antigravity

Install the desktop build for your operating system and open an existing project rather than starting empty, so the agent has real code to learn from. Start with one agent and one clearly scoped task, then try running two in parallel on separate branches. For frontend work, ask the agent to verify changes in the browser before you review the diff.

## Google Antigravity FAQ

Q: Is Google Antigravity free?
A: Yes, Google Antigravity is free for individual developers with basic weekly rate limits, as of October 2026. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscriptions raise those limits.

Q: What is Google Antigravity used for?
A: Google Antigravity is used to build software with AI agents that plan, write, run and test code, through a desktop agent manager, an IDE, a CLI and a Python SDK.

Q: Does Google Antigravity replace Gemini CLI?
A: For unpaid and Google One users, yes. The Gemini CLI site states it was replaced by the Antigravity CLI for those users on June 18, 2026.

Q: Google Antigravity vs Cursor: which is better?
A: Google Antigravity is the better value for individuals because it is free and runs parallel agents, while Cursor offers more model choice and a more mature editor ecosystem.

cubic is an AI code review tool that reviews GitHub pull requests against your whole codebase and your team's own rules for engineering teams that merge a lot of code. It also tries to cut the time between a comment and a fix by handing its findings directly to coding agents.

## What is cubic used for?

Teams use cubic as a first reviewer on every PR, so human reviewers spend their time on design questions instead of missed null checks. It also works earlier in the loop through a CLI and later through scheduled scans.

- Leaving inline review comments on each pull request, including cross-repository breakage
- Enforcing team rules written in plain English or learned from senior engineers' past review comments
- Scoring each PR's merge safety from 1 to 5 and auto-approving low-risk changes
- Writing PR descriptions automatically
- Passing review comments to Claude Code, Codex or Cursor so an agent applies the fix
- Running scheduled codebase scans that find bugs and security issues and open tickets for their owners

## Who cubic is best for

cubic suits startups and mid-size engineering teams on GitHub that ship many PRs a day, especially teams already using AI coding agents and seeing review become the bottleneck. Open-source maintainers can use it free on public repositories. Teams on GitLab or Bitbucket should confirm support first, since the site only describes GitHub, and solo developers with a handful of PRs a month may be fine on the free Starter plan or a lighter tool.

## cubic pricing

As of October 2026, cubic offers a free Starter plan with 20 PR reviews a month and free use on public repositories. Paid plans are billed per developer: Team is $30 per month billed yearly ($40 month to month) with 40,000 reviewed lines, auto-fix and five custom review agents; Pro is $79 per month billed yearly ($99 monthly) and adds codebase scans for three repositories, more custom agents, Confluence and MCP integrations, and an API; Max is $160 per month billed yearly ($200 monthly) with the highest line and auto-fix limits. Paid plans come with a 7-day trial. Every plan includes AI PR reviews, automatic PR descriptions and custom context.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Reviewed-line caps apply on each paid tier
- The site only documents GitHub integration

Greptile also leans on full-codebase context and is a close head-to-head comparison worth trialing side by side. Graphite is a better fit if you want stacked PRs and a faster review workflow, with AI review as one part of it. Qodo is broader, covering test generation and IDE help as well as review. Pick cubic when learned team rules, merge scoring and agent hand-off are what you want from a reviewer.

## Tips for getting started with cubic

Install it on one active repository first and leave it in comment-only mode for a week before enabling auto-approval. Seed the rules with a few plain-English conventions your team actually argues about, such as error handling or logging. Try the trick of replacing github.com with cubic.dev in a PR link to open the review view. Once you trust the comments, connect your coding agent so fixes arrive as commits rather than to-do items.

## cubic FAQ

Q: Is cubic free?

Q: Does cubic work with GitLab?

Q: Can cubic fix the issues it finds?

Q: What is the best alternative to cubic?
A: CodeRabbit is the most common alternative for AI pull request reviews, and Greptile is a close match for codebase-aware reviews.

It also fits teams using AI coding agents, since it plugs into Claude Code, Copilot and Codex. Very large enterprises with a mature, heavily customized scanning program may want to run it alongside existing tools before switching.

## Corgea pricing

As of October 2026, Corgea's free plan includes AI SAST, logic and auth scanning, and dependency, secrets, container and IaC scanning for up to two team members and ten repositories, with ten PR scans a month. Growth costs $39 per developer per month, adds PR scanning, code quality, the Corgea Agent, Jira and license enforcement, allows 100 repositories and requires at least five seats. Scale costs $49 per developer per month with a 20-seat minimum and adds custom and blocking rules, reporting, team management and APIs. Enterprise is custom and adds SSO, SCIM, single-tenant deployment and audit logs. Growth has a 14-day trial with no credit card. A seat counts contributors active in the last 90 days.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Seat minimums on paid plans mean a five-person team pays for at least five seats
- AI-suggested fixes still need human review before merging
- Claims of higher true positive rates and fix accuracy come from the vendor
- The site does not list supported languages in detail, so confirm coverage for your stack

## Corgea vs alternatives

Snyk is the established choice with a large vulnerability database and broad language support, and it is the safer pick for enterprises standardizing on one security vendor. Codacy combines code quality and security checks across many languages and suits teams that want one dashboard for both. CodeRabbit reviews pull requests broadly, including some security issues, but is not a dedicated security scanner. Corgea wins when you want AI that catches logic and authorization flaws and hands developers a ready-made fix.

## Tips for getting started with Corgea

Start on the free plan with one or two important repositories and compare its findings with your current scanner. Look closely at the business logic and auth findings, since those are where AI SAST differs most from pattern-based tools. Install the IDE extension so developers see issues before they open a pull request. When moving to a paid plan, enable PR scanning first and blocking rules later, once the team trusts the results.

## Corgea FAQ

Q: Is Corgea free?
A: Yes, Corgea has a free plan for up to two team members and ten repositories with AI SAST and dependency, secrets and IaC scanning. Paid plans start at $39 per developer per month.

Q: What does Corgea scan?
A: Corgea scans source code with AI SAST plus dependencies, secrets, containers and infrastructure as code, and also offers AI pentesting and design reviews.

Q: Does Corgea work with GitLab and Azure DevOps?
A: Yes, Corgea integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket and Harness, as well as IDEs such as VS Code and IntelliJ.

Q: What is the best alternative to Corgea?
A: Snyk is the best-known alternative for developer security scanning, and Codacy is a good option if you also want code quality checks.

## What is ZeroPath used for?

Companies use ZeroPath as their main code security scanner or alongside an existing one to catch higher-impact bugs. It covers several layers of AppSec in one product.

- Running AI SAST that targets business logic flaws and broken auth
- Verifying exploitability and generating patches that are meant to pass tests and merge cleanly
- Triaging dependency CVEs by whether your code actually calls the vulnerable function
- Detecting and validating exposed secrets and flagging IaC misconfigurations in Terraform, CloudFormation and Kubernetes

ZeroPath fits product security teams at growth-stage and enterprise companies, fintech and crypto firms where logic bugs are costly, and security consultancies. ## ZeroPath pricing

Q: What makes ZeroPath different from traditional SAST?

name: AI2SQL
tagline: Turn plain-English questions into SQL for your own schema, then explain, fix and optimize it
description: AI2SQL is a text-to-SQL tool that writes queries from plain English using your real tables and columns, and explains, fixes, formats and optimizes SQL for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake and more.
longDescription: AI2SQL is an AI SQL assistant for people who need queries but do not want to write them from scratch. You describe the result you want, and it generates SQL in the right dialect using your actual table and column names. It also explains existing queries clause by clause, fixes syntax and column errors, rewrites slow queries with notes such as missing indexes, and formats code consistently. On Pro and Team plans it connects to your own database through read-only connections and a desktop connector for Windows and macOS, so credentials stay on your machine, and a guard blocks writes and DDL. It also works as an MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. It supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, MongoDB, SQLite and Firebird. Plans start at $9 a month.

cons: Connecting your own database requires Pro or Team

moreContext:
AI2SQL is a text-to-SQL tool that turns plain-English questions into SQL queries for analysts, developers and business users who work with databases. What makes it more useful than pasting a question into a general chatbot is schema awareness: it writes SQL with your real table and column names in the correct dialect, then lets you run it safely against a read-only connection. It also covers the rest of the query lifecycle, from explaining an inherited query to tuning a slow one.

## What is AI2SQL used for?

People use AI2SQL to get answers from a database faster, learn SQL by seeing it explained, or clean up queries written by someone else.

- Generating SQL from a plain-English description of the result you want
- Explaining an existing query clause by clause
- Fixing syntax errors, dialect mismatches and wrong column names with an explanation
- Optimizing slow queries and suggesting indexes
- Running queries against a live, read-only connection and viewing the rows
- Using AI2SQL as an MCP server so Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor can write SQL against your schema

## Who AI2SQL is best for

AI2SQL suits data analysts, product managers, marketers and support staff who need occasional queries, junior developers learning SQL, and small teams that want a shared SQL helper without a full BI platform. Its Team plan adds a shared workspace and data masking for AI agents. Data teams that need governed dashboards and a semantic layer for the whole company will want a BI or analytics platform instead.

## AI2SQL pricing

As of October 2026, AI2SQL's FAQ mentions a free plan with three SQL queries a day on a demo database. Paid plans are Start at $9 per month (100 queries a month, basic model), Pro at $19 per month (unlimited queries, advanced model, your own database, read-only live queries from AI tools, API keys and the desktop app) and Team at $39 per month for five users with a shared workspace and data masking. Annual billing lowers these to $84, $168 and $348 a year. A $29 one-time Lifetime option offers 500 AI queries a month. Paid plans include a 7-day free trial. The pricing page is inconsistent about which databases the Start plan covers, so confirm before buying.

## Limitations to keep in mind

- Generated SQL still needs a sanity check, especially joins and filters on unfamiliar data
- Live connections are limited to PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server
- The free option only runs against a demo database
- It writes and runs queries but does not build dashboards or reports

## AI2SQL vs alternatives

ChatGPT can write SQL from a pasted schema and is fine for one-off questions, but it does not connect to your database or block unsafe statements by default. Julius AI is better if you want to upload data files and get charts and analysis rather than SQL. Hex suits data teams that want notebooks, SQL and AI together with sharing and apps. Programming Helper is a simple free option for quick query snippets. AI2SQL wins when you want schema-aware SQL, safe read-only execution and an MCP connection at a low monthly price.

## Tips for getting started with AI2SQL

Use the trial on the Pro plan so you can connect a read-only replica of a real database. Ask questions with the business terms your team uses, then check the generated joins against your schema. Use the explain feature on a few long legacy queries to see how well it reads your data model. If you use Claude or Cursor, set up the MCP server so they can query your schema directly.

## AI2SQL FAQ

Q: Is AI2SQL free?
A: AI2SQL's FAQ describes a free plan with three queries a day on a demo database. Paid plans start at $9 per month with a 7-day free trial.

Q: Which databases does AI2SQL support?
A: AI2SQL supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, Snowflake, BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, MongoDB, SQLite and Firebird for writing queries.

Q: Is AI2SQL safe to connect to a production database?
A: AI2SQL connects read-only by default and blocks writes, DDL and multi-statement input, but connecting to a read replica is still the safer choice.

Q: What is the best alternative to AI2SQL?
A: ChatGPT works for occasional SQL help, while Julius AI and Hex are better for analysis and visualization beyond writing queries.
